A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully evolved a lead inhibitor into a dual mode inhibitor with improved LLE.

we have designed and synthesized inhibitors with increased affinity and improved lipophilic ligands efficiencies by adding weak zinc binding fragments to an initial inhibitor with allosteric binding mode.
we were able to design and synthesize novel MMP-13 inhibitors with improved potency and LLE by using a structure-based approach and by introducing zinc binding groups to the inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a zinc binding fragment to a weakly zinc binding inhibitor can increase the affinity of a ligand and improve its LLE.

the addition of zinc binding fragments to a lead molecule can be a successful strategy to improve the affinity and LLE of an allosteric inhibitor, which can lead to the discovery of new and more potent MMP inhibitors.
the addition of weak zinc binding fragments to an allosterically binding inhibitor is a feasible strategy to increase the affinity and improve the lipophilic efficiency of such compounds.
